full_judgment:
2. This rule is directed against order No.32 dated 4-4-2012 passed in Money Execution Case No.2 of 20 11 by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet whereby further proceedings of Execution Case No.2 of 2012 was stayed by the learned Joint District Judge in consideration of pendency of Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2011 initiated in connection with the self-same execution case under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure, at the instance of the 3rd party. 

 3. Facts giving rise to this rule in a nutshell are that the opposite-party No.2 offered to sell her only property through her attorney and the petitioner accepted the offer of sale at a consideration of Taka 1,13,10,000 and an agreement for sale was executed in between the petitioner and the opposite-party No.2 through her attorney on payment of Taka 80 (eighty) lakhs by the petitioner to the opposite-party No.2 but eventually deed of transfer could not be executed by the opposite-party No. 2 therefore, the opposite-party No. 2 paid back the money received by her by two cheques one for Taka 30 (thirty) lakhs and the other one for Taka 50 (fifty) lacs. The said two cheques were placed before the bank by the petitioner but those were bounced. Therefore, the petitioner took recourse to the provision of Negotiable Instruments Act upon bringing two CR Cases before the court concerned which were eventually sent to the court of Sessions for trial and two sessions cases were registered thereupon. After trial in both the said Sessions Cases the opposite-party No.2 was convicted by the learned Sessions Judge by his order dated 19-10-2010 and sentencing her to suffer imprisonment for one year under section 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act with a fine of Taka 50+50= 1,00,00,000 ( one) crore in Sessions Case No. 604 of 2009 the opposite-party No.2 obtained bail during pendency of the Sessions Case No. 604 of 2009 but remained in abscondence at the trial, therefore, the judgments were passed in absentia. Thereafter, the opposite-party No.2 could neither be apprehend nor there was any scope for realization of fine as such the petitioner through government invoked section 386 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for realization of fine amount and execution case No.2 of 2011 was registered before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for realization of fine and in the said Execution Case the said property was attached. During pendency of the said execution case the opposite- party No. 1 tiled application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure claiming itself to be a donee of the land in question, since according to him the land in question was gifted in favour of the deity, and the opposite-party No.1 and the deity is in possession thereof. 

 4. Upon the said application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2011 was registered by the learned Joint District Judge, thereafter the opposite-party No.1 filed an application in execution case No.2 of 20 II praying for stay of further proceedings of the said execution case which after hearing was allowed by the learned Joint District Judge by his order No. 32 dated 4-4-12 which is in challenge before this court. 

 5. We have heard the learned Advocates from both sides, perused the petition and other materials on record including the impugned order. On a scrutiny of the impugned order we find that the learned Joint District Judge has stayed further proceedings of the execution case No.2 of 2011 in view of the tiling of the application under order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the 3rd party the opposite-party No.1 but in doing so the learned Joint District Judge did not assign any reason which was expected of him rather in a slipshod manner the order has been passed presumably in view of sub-rule (2) of Rule 58 of Order, XXI. It has also been brought to our notice by way of supplementary affidavit that the land in question was not only gifted in favour of the deity by the opposite-party No.2 but the deity in turn has also registered another document allowing the daughter of the opposite-party No.2 to remain in possession and enjoyment of the land in question. 

 6. These are things however to be scrutinized by the learned Joint District Judge while conducting an investigation in the Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2011 brought under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 8. Accordingly, this rule is disposed of with a direction upon the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet to conclude the investigation under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure brought by the opposite-party No.1 in Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2011 within 6(six) months from the date receipt of this order from this court particularly with reference to the proviso to sub-rule (1) of rule 58 of Order XXI, CPC. Meanwhile, further proceedings of the Execution Case in question shall remain suspended but in the event of any unnecessary delay if caused by the opposite-party No. 1 the learned Joint District Judge shall be at liberty to proceed with the Execution case in accordance with law. 

 9. Since the aforesaid direction has been made at the instance of the petitioner Ranju Chandra Das his presence may also be necessary in the proceeding of Miscellaneous Case No. 28 of 2011 before the Joint District Judge if he is so advised.
